verdicts.reason: Critique handling: both share the loss-conditioned, length-matched two-order gate, but Y answers X's own listed failures by drawing the verifier from outside the final panel's family, adding an ambition guard and a reason filter, replaying the same opponents, and stating explicit kill thresholds.

Evidence/testability: both use the same expected-max portfolio selection, but Y fits tau from saved rating residuals, excludes under-compared items that would otherwise be picked for variance, gates on label agreement (kappa), and pre-registers kill criteria, whereas X's tau is an arbitrary 0.5 SD.

Mechanism robustness: X's strongest point is closing the persuasive-prose channel with executable checks, but Y also blocks rigged checks with a witness value that must flip the outcome, normalises the score over load-bearing claims, and tests on 10 briefs against the single agent with kill thresholds instead of X's single-brief test.

Fit to brief/test design: both share the bounded repair loop and template library, but Y re-extracts claims so developers cannot weaken them unnoticed (load-bearing flag), controls for matched prose feedback, and makes a blinded panel win rate against the single agent the primary outcome, while X measures only falsified-claim rate on one brief.

Mechanism correctness: the cards are nearly identical, but Y re-ranks the finals on fresh comparisons, which avoids winner's-curse inflation from selecting on the same judgements used to accept mutants, and it adds a kill threshold on the held-out child-beats-parent rate.

Answer to the Goodhart critique: both specify the same residual selection head, but Y fits on one panel family and scores on another with a bootstrap kill rule, which tests the listed failure mode directly; X labels with a single panel and so risks learning that panel's biases.

Testability: the mechanisms are identical, but Y's test uses leave-one-brief-out refits, separates reliability weighting from boundary allocation in a factorial ablation, sets a tau-based kill rule, and caps any one judge's share at 40%, which limits dependence on noisy a_j estimates.

Statistical validity: X's power claim treats about 540 correlated contests as independent, whereas Y analyses per-brief rates paired by brief, sets a kill rule on that interval, and shrinks toward each operator's global win rate instead of a flat prior.

Critique handling and fit to brief: Y's two-family 4/4 gate plus a same-length paraphrase placebo measures and bounds style bias in the gate, and its primary outcome is the benchmark comparison against the single agent's top 3, while X measures only acceptance rate and revised-versus-original preference and leaves verifier-panel family overlap unaddressed.

Mechanism safety: Y derives tau from measured within-cluster correlation, rejects swaps that lower the expected mean-of-3 by more than 1 SE, reduces exactly to top-3 when finalists are diverse, and adds win rate against the single agent as a metric, removing X's acknowledged mean-of-3 downside.

Fit to brief: Y adds codebase probes that decide the brief's own 'implementable in this codebase' claims, measures the checkable fraction in a cheap step-0 kill test, and assigns low-checkability cards the pool median rather than last place, fixing X's admitted penalty on qualitative ideas.

Implementability and test design: Y runs standalone by extracting claims itself when no ledger exists, caps extra development tokens at 40%, reverts over-struck cards to the original, and makes blinded win rate against the single agent a kill criterion, while X depends on another card's ledger and tests on a single brief with proxy outcomes only.

Answer to the overfitting critique: Y accepts variants with a gate family that is neither the ranker's nor the panel's, shows the gate only length-normalised fields, and measures the overfit gap against a held-out family with explicit kill thresholds, whereas X only suggests a family split as mitigation.

Robustness with scarce data: Y's within-run conditional logit removes between-brief effects, and its first stage frees only sign-constrained nuisance weights so it needs about 5 briefs rather than 15, and an oracle-headroom kill test is added, all directly answering X's listed heterogeneity and Goodhart failures.

Evidence efficiency: Y calibrates position, self-preference and a shared verbosity term with label-free probes, so only a_j needs external verdicts (about 100 rather than 300), shrinks a_j toward a common value, and adds a bias-only ablation with a kill rule.

Testability and self-containment: Y defines its own two-order, length-capped, other-family contest rule instead of depending on card 0, warm-starts from saved finalists, and runs a cheap offline stage-1 kill test (chi-square on operator win rates, leave-one-brief-out log-loss) before the costly online arm.
